newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arboyne says Nonoc costs may rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arboyne says Nonoc costs may rise.

text.p: The cost of refurbishing the giant Nonoc nickel mine in the Philippines could rise to more than US$500 million if a range of new options are included, Perth-based miner Arboyne NL said on Thursday.
Arboyne has previously estimated it would cost about US$370 million to rehabilitate the operation, which was one of the world's 10 biggest nickel refineries before closing in 1986.

"The directors are considering a number of options including enhancing the process to maximise recovery and throughput, modernising the power plant, blending imported and domestic ore, installing a cobalt plant and de-bottlenecking the refinery," Arboyne said in a statement.
"If all these options are incorporated they will have a significant effect on the refurbishment capital expenditure budget which would then be in excess of US$500 million."
Nonoc, which is capable of producing 65 million pounds of metal a year, was hit by low metal pricecs, high energy costs, a devalued Philippine peso and high interest rates.
Arboyne in November appointed ING Barings and McIntosh Corporate Ltd to raise funding for the project.
Merrill Lynch, which has taken over McIntosh & Co Ltd, had agreed to proceed with the capital raising, and would act as joint global co-ordinator with ING Barings, it said.
Arboyne said in January it planned to raise up to US$20 million by a convertible note issue for pre-refurbishment work.
